title: Euler dimension and equivariant trace identities for finite multigraphs
statement:
Let $V,E$ be finite sets, with each $e\in E$ having an unordered pair of distinct endpoints in $V$; parallel edges are allowed. Choose orientations and put $C_1=\mathbf Q^E$, $C_0=\mathbf Q^V$, $\partial(e)=t(e)-s(e)$, and $Z_1=\ker(\partial:C_1\to C_0)$, where $\mathbf Q^S$ is the vector space with basis $S$. Let $\pi_0$ be the set of equivalence classes of vertices for the equivalence relation generated by the endpoint pairs, and set $c=|\pi_0|$ (zero if $V$ is empty). For a permutation $\sigma$ of vertices and edges preserving endpoints, let $T_0$ be its permutation operator on $C_0$, $T_1$ its signed permutation operator on $C_1$ (negative when orientation is reversed), and $T_Z$ the restriction of $T_1$ to $Z_1$. Write $f_0$ for the number of fixed vertices, $f_+$ for the number of fixed edges with each endpoint fixed, $f_-$ for the number of fixed edges with endpoints interchanged, and $f_c$ for the number of connected components preserved setwise by $\sigma$. With traces defined as sums of diagonal matrix entries [def-weil-endomorphism-trace],
$$\dim_{\mathbf Q} Z_1=|E|-|V|+c,\qquad f_0-f_++f_-=f_c-\operatorname{tr}(T_Z\mid Z_1).$$
The dimension equality is an equality of integers. Both formulas hold without any connectedness, degree or trivial-action assumption.

proof.text: Put $H=\mathbf Q^{\pi_0}$ and define $p:C_0\to H$ by $p(v)=[v]$ on vertex basis vectors. It is surjective: every component contains a vertex. Each $p\partial(e)$ is zero since the endpoints belong to one component. Conversely, choose a vertex $r_D$ in each component $D$. Every $v\in D$ is joined to $r_D$ by a finite sequence of edges: finite edge paths form an equivalence relation containing the endpoint pairs, and their endpoints lie in the generated relation, so these relations agree. The signed sum of the edges of such a path has boundary $v-r_D$, by cancellation of consecutive vertices. If $x=\sum_v a_vv$ has $p(x)=0$, then $\sum_{v\in D}a_v=0$ for every $D$, and hence $x=\sum_D\sum_{v\in D}a_v(v-r_D)$ belongs to $B=\operatorname{im}\partial$. Thus $B=\ker p$, including when $V$ is empty.

proof.text: The displayed finite bases of $C_1,C_0,H$ make them finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. The subspace assertion of [lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension], applied to $Z_1\subseteq C_1$ and $B\subseteq C_0$, makes $Z_1$ and $B$ finite-dimensional too. The inclusion $Z_1\to C_1$ is injective, $\partial:C_1\to B$ is surjective by the definition of image, and its kernel is exactly $Z_1$ by definition. The inclusion $B\to C_0$ is injective, $p$ is surjective by step 1, and its kernel is $B$ by step 1. These are the two short exact sequences $0\to Z_1\to C_1\to B\to0$ and $0\to B\to C_0\to H\to0$.

proof.text: Let $T_H$ permute the basis of $H$ by the induced permutation of components. This permutation is well-defined because applying $\sigma$, or its inverse, to an edge path again gives an edge path. On each oriented edge $e$, $\partial T_1(e)=\sigma(t(e))-\sigma(s(e))=T_0\partial(e)$: reversing the chosen orientation of $\sigma(e)$ accounts for exactly the minus sign in $T_1$. Thus $T_0$ preserves $B$ and $T_1$ preserves $Z_1$. Write $T_B=T_0|_B$. On vertex basis vectors $pT_0(v)=[\sigma(v)]=T_Hp(v)$, and the other two intertwining identities are those of restriction. Therefore the two sequences in step 2 have compatible endomorphisms $(T_Z,T_1,T_B)$ and $(T_B,T_0,T_H)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-trace-exact] to each sequence in step 2 with the endomorphisms from step 3; injectivity, surjectivity, exactness, finite-dimensionality, and both intertwining identities have all been verified. It gives $\operatorname{tr}T_1=\operatorname{tr}T_Z+\operatorname{tr}T_B$ and $\operatorname{tr}T_0=\operatorname{tr}T_B+\operatorname{tr}T_H$. Subtracting cancels $\operatorname{tr}T_B$, so $\operatorname{tr}T_0-\operatorname{tr}T_1=\operatorname{tr}T_H-\operatorname{tr}T_Z$.

proof.text: Compute the three traces in their displayed bases using [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. The diagonal coefficient of $T_0$ at $v$ is $1$ if $\sigma(v)=v$ and $0$ otherwise, giving $\operatorname{tr}T_0=f_0$. Likewise $\operatorname{tr}T_H=f_c$. The diagonal coefficient of $T_1$ at $e$ is zero unless $\sigma(e)=e$. For a fixed edge, its two distinct endpoints are either individually fixed, giving coefficient $+1$, or interchanged, giving coefficient $-1$; these exhaust the permutations of its endpoint pair. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}T_1=f_+-f_-$. Substitution into step 4 gives the required trace identity.

source.place: Printed p.87, final paragraph of the graph argument following Lemma 1.17; explicit chain-space argument supplied by Q103 (primary PDF read online, local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Apply the trace identity just proved to the identity permutation of this same graph. Then $f_0=|V|$, $f_+=|E|$, $f_-=0$, $f_c=c$, and $T_Z$ is the identity. In any finite basis the identity matrix has diagonal entries all $1$, so [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] and the basis-cardinality definition [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] give $\operatorname{tr}T_Z=\dim_{\mathbf Q}Z_1$. Hence $|V|-|E|=c-\dim_{\mathbf Q}Z_1$ in $\mathbf Q$. All four quantities are integers; injectivity of $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$ and rearrangement give $\dim_{\mathbf Q}Z_1=|E|-|V|+c$ as an equality of integers. For $V=\varnothing$, distinct endpoints force $E=\varnothing$; every space above is zero and both identities read $0=0$.

lean.statement: theorem euler_trace (V : Type u) (E : Type v) [Finite V] [Finite E] (s t : E → V) (_hne : ∀ e : E, s e ≠ t e) (σV : Equiv.Perm V) (σE : Equiv.Perm E) (hσ : ∀ e : E, (σV (s e) = s (σE e) ∧ σV (t e) = t (σE e)) ∨ (σV (s e) = t (σE e) ∧ σV (t e) = s (σE e))) : (Module.finrank ℚ (LinearMap.ker (boundary s t)) : ℤ) = (Nat.card E : ℤ) - (Nat.card V : ℤ) + (Nat.card (Quot (fun x y : V ↦ ∃ e : E, s e = x ∧ t e = y)) : ℤ) ∧ (Nat.card {x : V // σV x = x} : ℚ) - (Nat.card {e : E // σE e = e ∧ σV (s e) = s e ∧ σV (t e) = t e} : ℚ) + (Nat.card {e : E // σE e = e ∧ σV (s e) = t e ∧ σV (t e) = s e} : ℚ) = (Nat.card {C : Quot (fun x y : V ↦ ∃ e : E, s e = x ∧ t e = y) // ∀ x : V, Quot.mk _ x = C → Quot.mk _ (σV x) = C} : ℚ) - LinearMap.trace ℚ (LinearMap.ker (boundary s t)) (cycleMap s t σV σE hσ)
